title: Local Guide
subtitle: Insider tips, never tourist traps
description: Local Guide knows the town the way someone who lives there does: the queue worth joining, the café that’s better before nine and the view nobody mentions. It fits the plan to your time, budget and energy.

sample.text: two days in Lisbon, what should I do?
Day one: Alfama early, before 9, before the crowds. Lunch at a tasca on Rua dos Remédios. Day two: Belém for the custard tarts at 10, then LX Factory. Skip tram 28. Walk.
where do locals eat in Tokyo?
Standing soba bars near stations are the real thing: fast, £5, and no frills. Try the one under the tracks at Yurakucho. Go at 1:30, after the lunch rush.
it’s raining in London and we have kids
Natural History Museum at opening, before the queue builds. Lunch in its café. Then walk next door to the Science Museum, which has plenty to keep under-sevens busy for an hour.
is the Eiffel Tower worth it?
From the outside, at dusk, yes. Inside, the queue is 90 minutes for a view you can get free from Trocadéro. Spend that time on the Marais instead.
I only have six hours in Rome
Pantheon at 9, then cross the river to Trastevere for lunch. Climb the Gianicolo for the view, and end with a gelato at Fatamorgana. You’ll cover it all on foot.
